title: Golden Hour Photography: Times, Settings and Portrait Tips — cv.cm
description: What golden hour and blue hour are, why their length depends on latitude and season, how to find the times, and camera and phone settings for warm light.
h1: What is golden hour in photography, and when is it?
answer: Golden hour is the time shortly after sunrise and shortly before sunset when the sun is low, roughly within 6 degrees of the horizon. Light passes through more air, so it turns warm, soft and directional, with long shadows. It lasts about 20 minutes near the equator and close to an hour or more at higher latitudes, so check exact times for your place and date.

sections.h: Why the light changes when the sun is low
body: At midday the sun is high, light comes from above, and it is hard and white. Faces get dark eye sockets and bright foreheads, and colors look flat. When the sun drops toward the horizon, three things change at once.

ul: Color: sunlight travels through much more atmosphere. Blue light is scattered away, so what reaches you is warmer, more yellow, orange and finally red.
Softness: the light is weaker and partly scattered, so shadows have gentler edges and contrast is lower. A face can be lit from the front without squinting.
Direction: light comes from the side, so it shows shape and texture. Shadows become long and add depth to landscapes.

body: In numbers, midday daylight is often described as about 5,500 K. Golden hour light is much warmer, roughly 3,000 to 4,000 K, and the last minutes before sunset can be warmer still. Brightness also drops, from around EV 15 in full sun to about EV 10 to 12 in golden hour, which is still enough to shoot handheld.

body: The 6-degree limits are photographers' working definitions, not official ones. Weather services define civil twilight precisely: it ends when the center of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, nautical twilight at 12 degrees and astronomical twilight at 18 degrees. Blue hour falls mostly inside civil twilight and is short, often 10 to 30 minutes, so be set up before sunset.

sections.h: How long golden hour lasts where you live
body: Golden hour is not always one hour. Its length depends on how steeply the sun crosses the horizon, and that depends on your latitude and the season.

ul: Near the equator (for example Singapore, Jakarta, Quito): the sun goes almost straight down, about 15 degrees per hour. Dropping 6 degrees takes about 24 minutes, and golden hour and twilight are both short.
Mid-latitudes (for example Tokyo, Seoul, Madrid, Beijing, New York): the sun sets at an angle, so the same 6 degrees takes roughly 30 to 50 minutes depending on the season.

High latitudes (for example Scandinavia, Scotland, northern Canada): in summer the sun slides along the horizon and golden light can last for hours. In winter the sun may stay low all day, giving soft light even at noon.

body: Weather changes everything. A clear horizon gives warm direct light. Thick clouds on the horizon can end golden hour early, while broken clouds above can turn bright red after the sun sets. Mountains or tall buildings to the west also make your local sunset earlier than the official time.

sections.h: How to find golden hour times

ol: Look up sunrise and sunset for your exact location and date. Many phone weather apps show them. Official calculators such as the NOAA Solar Calculator or the U.S. Naval Observatory sun and moon data also give the sun's elevation and civil twilight times.
For an evening shoot, start about 60 minutes before sunset at mid-latitudes, or about 30 minutes before near the equator.
For a morning shoot, arrive during civil twilight, before sunrise, and keep shooting for about an hour after.

Check the direction of the sun. Sunset is in the west-northwest in local summer and the west-southwest in local winter (reversed in the Southern Hemisphere). A map app compass helps you plan where the light will come from.
Check the forecast and the horizon. Low cloud on the western horizon means less direct sun for an evening shoot.

body.note: Plan to arrive 30 minutes early. Most golden hour shoots fail because people are still parking or changing clothes when the light is best.

body: White balance matters most. Auto white balance often tries to remove the orange glow, which makes golden hour look like ordinary daylight. Set daylight (sunny) or shade to keep the warmth, or shoot RAW and set it later. Shade gives an even warmer result.
The light fades quickly near sunset. Use auto ISO with a minimum shutter speed, for example 1/250 s for portraits, so the camera raises ISO rather than letting the shutter get too slow.

ul: Tap the face or subject on the screen to set focus and exposure there. If the sky blows out to white, drag the brightness slider down a little.
Lock focus and exposure (press and hold on iPhone for AE/AF Lock, tap Lock on Pixel) when you want to recompose.
Use the 2x or 3x lens for portraits. It makes the background larger and the face more natural.
Portrait mode blurs the background and makes the sun into soft circles of light.
Turn off the flash for warm light on the face; use it only for a backlit subject if you cannot get the face bright enough any other way.
When you edit, resist the urge to add more warmth or saturation. Skin turns orange quickly.

sections.h: Portrait tips and planning a golden hour shoot

ol: Choose two or three spots within a short walk. You will not have time to drive between locations.
Start with front or side light while the sun is still higher, then move to backlight as it gets lower.
Place the sun behind the subject's head or shoulder for a rim of light in the hair. Use a hand, a hood or a tree to keep the sun from hitting the lens directly.
Bounce light back into the face with a white reflector, a white wall, or even a light-colored shirt.
Shoot the warmest sunset frames last, then switch to blue hour images with city lights or a lamp.
Check rules before the shoot. Some parks, beaches and landmarks require a permit for professional or commercial photography, and popular spots are crowded at sunset.

body.note: Never look at the sun through an optical viewfinder or a long lens, even at sunset. Compose with the rear screen and keep the sun at the edge of the frame or behind the subject.

faq.q: What time is golden hour today?
faq.a: It depends on your location and date. Look up today's sunset time and start about an hour before it at mid-latitudes, or about 30 minutes before near the equator. The morning golden hour starts at sunrise.

faq.q: Is golden hour better in the morning or evening?
faq.a: The light is similar. Mornings are often clearer and quieter, with mist or dew and fewer people. Evenings are easier to plan and often have more haze, which can make the light warmer.

faq.q: Does golden hour happen on cloudy days?
faq.a: Only if there is a gap near the horizon where the sun can shine through. With full cloud cover you get soft but not warm light. Broken clouds can produce strong color just after sunset.

faq.q: What is the difference between golden hour and magic hour?
faq.a: Usually nothing. Magic hour is another name for golden hour, used often by filmmakers. Some people use it to include the blue hour as well.

faq.q: What white balance should I use for sunset photos?
faq.a: Daylight or sunny white balance keeps the warm color you see. Auto white balance may cool it down, and the shade or cloudy preset makes it warmer.
